command: python3 scripts/test-routing-e2e.py (second run reused the image via --skip-build after a transient Docker daemon 502 aborted the first run's V2 bring-up; the aborted run's completed phases also passed)
environment: private MySQL Compose project with real service binaries, mock upstream, Redis, and Prometheus
result: PASS all eight phases; private containers, network, and volumes removed
purpose: Attribute the Redis-outage dependency-RPC latency increase left open by o5-redis-fault-isolated-retest-2026-09-27 ('identity-side Redis fallback path not attributed'). Adds server-side handling P95 (newly wired xgrpc.MetricsUnaryServerInterceptor with 1ms/2.5ms buckets), per-instance process CPU rate, and max goroutines to each O5a window. Attribution queries use a look-back widened by one scrape interval because burst windows are bracketed by relay scrapes only.

review_correction.status: Historical observations only; server/CPU/goroutine windows are not valid for causal attribution. Full Compose acceptance was not rerun during review.
review_correction.reason: Only relay scrapes bracketed the burst. Widening the start by 15s neither waits for a dependency's post-burst scrape nor excludes preceding setup traffic. Missing channel baseline and billing outage samples cannot be replaced by recovered or client-side measurements.
review_correction.fix: The reviewed sampler waits for all four targets and queries each target between its own successful pre/post-burst scrapes. Query failures and missing server samples for measured client methods now fail acceptance.
review_correction.code_commit_note: code_commit identifies the original pre-review run, retained on codex/review-four-backup-20260929; windows above were not regenerated by the corrected sampler.

attribution.observed_latency: The original run reported identity server P95 1.68 -> 4.67 -> 1.60 ms, channel outage/recovered 2.49/0.98 ms with no baseline, and billing client P95 0.95 ms. These unsynchronized windows are retained for traceability, not a validated server/client comparison.
attribution.db_path_correction: For the V2 legacy-token path, GetAuthSnapshot performs five SELECTs: token, user, then user/token/grants in GetRoutingFacts. GetRoutingGroup performs four SELECTs: group, channels, accounts, model grants, plus transaction overhead and possible schema probes. Counting repo calls as SQL reads produced the incorrect ~3/~1 claim; no proportionality or DB duration was measured.
attribution.process_pressure: The recorded averages and sampled goroutine maxima show no sustained process-pressure increase in those windows. They cannot exclude brief retry/reconnect activity, and the windows require correction before comparison.
attribution.identity_has_no_redis_on_path: Code inspection of GetAuthSnapshot -> ValidateToken/FindTokenByKey -> FindUserByID -> GetRoutingFacts finds MySQL reads and no Redis operation in this synchronous RPC path. Background Redis work can still contend for shared resources.
attribution.conclusion: The identity-internal Redis fallback hypothesis is unsupported by its call path. Shared MySQL/Docker-VM contention remains a hypothesis, not an established cause. Corrected sampling plus DB/host measurements or a controlled comparison are needed to attribute the latency increase. The production O5 suspension decision is unchanged.

boundaries: Server-side channel baseline and billing outage samples are missing; no complete three-window server comparison exists for either method.
Legacy healthy/recovered bursts had no measured GetAuthSnapshot RPC (L1 absorbed lookups), unchanged from the 2026-09-27 retest.
MySQL/Redis containers are not Prometheus targets; database latency and VM contention were not measured directly.
Server latency includes all statuses and callers; client P95 includes only relay OK calls. Valid comparisons require excluding other traffic and accounting for errors.
Breaker rejections now have a local counter regression check; rejection latency and production deployment remain unverified.
A natural production Redis incident can provide acceptance evidence only after availability, fallback, settlement, alert delivery and recovery are checked; an incident alone is not a pass.
Millisecond-scale numbers come from a shared laptop Docker VM and are not a production latency budget.
